prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1229; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you were involved in on a street in Pearland, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please describe in your own words what happened.

A: I was driving east on a two-lane road, going maybe thirty miles an hour. A car coming from the other direction drifted into my lane while making a left turn. I braked and steered right, but we still hit nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, but my airbags went off.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: How did you first notice you were hurt?

A: My right wrist hurt right away. I held it against the steering wheel when the airbag deployed. I didn't think much of it at first, but by evening it was swollen and I couldn't grip anything.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same night. They took X-rays and said I had a fracture in my wrist. I was referred to an orthopedic specialist and I'm wearing a splint now.

Q: Did you have any other injuries or pain in your neck or back?

A: My neck is a little sore, but nothing serious. The main problem is the wrist.

Q: Did the other driver say anything at the scene?

A: She said she was sorry and that she didn't see my car. She also said she was looking at her phone for a second.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want my car repaired and my wrist to heal properly.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
